title: How you communicate today, and how to choose

say: How you communicate today, and how to choose.
This is the video for Module 1 of Communication and Self-Expression: foundations.
Many arguments at home, in the market and in meetings do not start with bad intentions. They start with a message that arrived in a different shape in another person's mind.

say: Picture a tomato seller telling a regular buyer that prices went up. She is the sender.

panel.heading: How a message travels
items: Sender: the person with the idea or need
Message: what you said, not what you meant
Channel: face to face, call, voice note, text
Noise: outside, like traffic; inside, like worry
Feedback: the reply shows what arrived

say: She shouts, the basket is now more. That is the message. But how much more? The message is what you said, not what you meant.

Feedback: the reply shows what arrived

say: The channel was a quick shout across the stall, to a buyer rushing for a bus.

panel.heading: How a message travels

say: Noise can be outside, like traffic or a weak network. Or inside, like the buyer's worry about money. Inside noise is often the bigger problem.

panel.heading: How a message travels

say: The buyer frowns and says, you people just increase anyhow. That is feedback, and it is useful, because it shows exactly what arrived.

say: Face to face carries words, tone, face and body. Use it for feelings, disagreements, apologies and important requests to elders. A phone call keeps the tone but loses the face.

panel.heading: Feelings face to face, facts in writing
right: Not for anger or bad news

say: A text keeps only the words, so the reader adds her own tone, often a worse one than you meant. Use texts for times, amounts and addresses. And remember voice notes use more data than a short text.

panel.heading: Feelings face to face, facts in writing
right: Not for anger or bad news

say: For example, Ngozi is secretary of a savings group of 20 women in Enugu. She sends, meeting moved to Saturday. Six members come on the wrong day.

panel.heading: Fixing a savings group meeting time
items: Find the noise: which Saturday? read late?
Rewrite with date, time, place
Add: not this coming Saturday
Ask everyone to reply OK
Call the ones who did not reply

say: She finds the noise. Two Saturdays were possible, and some members only saw the preview late at night.

panel.heading: Fixing a savings group meeting time

Add: not this coming Saturday
Ask everyone to reply OK
Call the ones who did not reply

say: She rewrites it: Saturday 14th, 4pm, at Mama Chidi's shop. Not this coming Saturday.

say: She asks everyone to reply OK when they see it. After a day, 17 of 20 have replied.

say: She calls the 3 who did not reply, because a call reaches people the group chat does not.

say: The fix was not more words. It was specific words plus a feedback check. Ask warmly: just so I know I explained it well, what will you tell the others?

panel.rule: Close the loop: ask what they understood.

say: Your friend wants to borrow your gele, but has not returned the last one. A passive reply is, ok no wahala, while you are upset inside. It is respectful, but not honest.

panel.heading: Honest and respectful at the same time

cards.d: Respectful but not honest. 'Ok no wahala' while upset inside. Resentment builds.
Aggressive: honest, not respectful. Passive-aggressive: 'Hmm. Some people sha.'
Honest and respectful. 'I need the blue one back first. Can you bring it on Sunday?'

say: An aggressive reply in capital letters is honest, but not respectful. A passive-aggressive reply hides the anger in a hint, like, hmm, some people sha, or leaving her on read.

panel.heading: Honest and respectful at the same time

cards.d: Respectful but not honest. 'Ok no wahala' while upset inside. Resentment builds.
Aggressive: honest, not respectful. Passive-aggressive: 'Hmm. Some people sha.'
Honest and respectful. 'I need the blue one back first. Can you bring it on Sunday?'

say: An assertive reply is honest and respectful at the same time. I am happy to help, but I need the blue one back first. Can you bring it on Sunday?
You can keep your greetings and respect words like ma and sir. A quiet voice with a clear request is assertive.

say: Before a hard conversation, ask first: am I safe here?

panel.heading: Is now the right time to speak?
items: Am I safe here?
Am I calm enough?
Is the other person ready?
Speak now, or set a time

say: Am I calm enough? If you are very angry, say, let us talk about this tomorrow evening. Waiting with a set time is preparation, not avoidance.

panel.heading: Is now the right time to speak?
items: Am I safe here?
Am I calm enough?
Is the other person ready?
Speak now, or set a time

say: Is the other person ready, or are they rushed, drunk, or in front of an audience?

panel.heading: Is now the right time to speak?
items: Am I safe here?
Am I calm enough?
Is the other person ready?
Speak now, or set a time

say: Then speak, or plan a time.

panel.heading: Is now the right time to speak?
items: Am I safe here?

Is the other person ready?
Speak now, or set a time

say: If someone has hit, threatened or controlled you, this course's scripts are not the right tool, and the problem is not your communication.
Talk privately to someone you trust, a health worker, a women's support organisation or the police. Getting help is a strong act of self-expression.

panel.heading: Is now the right time to speak?
items: Am I safe here?
Am I calm enough?
Is the other person ready?
Speak now, or set a time
panel.rule: If someone frightens or harms you, seek help. Safety comes first.

say: To remember. A message is what you said, not what you meant. Match the channel to the message. Close the loop with a feedback check. Be honest and respectful together.
And when you rate yourself, choose a focus situation that happens often and carries medium risk, not the hardest relationship in your life.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A message is what you said, not what you meant
Feelings face to face; facts in writing
Close the loop with a warm feedback check
Assertive: honest and respectful together
Start with a frequent, medium-risk situation
